evidence: src/application/dtos.ts declares CreateProductDto, ProductDto, PlaceOrderDto and OrderDto, which both services use as their boundary types
src/application/catalogue-service.ts: CatalogueService(products: ProductRepository) with addProduct, listProducts and a private toDto(product): ProductDto
src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService(orders: OrderRepository, products: ProductRepository) passes transitions to order.advanceTo, order.cancel, product.reserve and product.release
src/application/order-service.ts: placeOrder checks `products[index].stock < items[index].quantity` for every item before any reserve call, a deliberate all-or-nothing pre-check
src/application/order-service.ts: the `if (!product) throw new NotFoundError(...)` lookup is repeated in placeOrder and cancelOrder, both inside the same file

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files form one application layer for the order and catalogue use cases. dtos.ts holds the boundary contracts. CatalogueService and OrderService take ProductRepository and OrderRepository through their constructors and return DTOs through private toDto mappers. Neither service reaches past its repositories or touches storage directly. State transitions go through the entity methods Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel, Product.reserve and Product.release, so they are not re-implemented in the services. Order lookup goes through one helper, requireOrder. Item normalisation lives in one place, combineItems. Three smaller points do not reach a fail. First, placeOrder pre-checks stock before calling Product.reserve. The comment says this keeps all-or-nothing reservation, but it may repeat a check inside Product.reserve, which I can't see because the domain files were not provided. Second, the product-not-found lookup is written out twice in OrderService, in placeOrder and cancelOrder, with no requireProduct helper. Third, the target union in advanceOrder is a hand-written list of states rather than one derived from OrderState. None of these splits the module, breaks its abstractions or clearly duplicates a rule across the unit.
